history.heading: A shared island
paragraphs: Saint Martin is the northern French part of an island in the northeastern Caribbean, the southern part being Sint Maarten, belonging to the Netherlands. It is the smallest inhabited island divided between two countries. Inhabited by Arawak and Kalinago peoples, the island was named by Columbus in 1493.

France and the Netherlands agreed to divide the island in the Treaty of Concordia in 1648; according to legend, the border was set by a Frenchman and a Dutchman walking around the island. Plantations of sugar and salt production used enslaved Africans until abolition in 1848 on the French side.

history.heading: Modern era
paragraphs: Part of Guadeloupe for a long time, Saint Martin became a separate French overseas collectivity in 2007. Hurricane Irma devastated the island in 2017.

culture.heading: Island culture
paragraphs: French is official, but English and an English-based Creole are widely spoken, along with Spanish and Haitian Creole among immigrants. The border with Sint Maarten is open, and the island shares a common culture. Grand Case is known as a gastronomic capital of the Caribbean.

politics.heading: French overseas collectivity
paragraphs: Saint Martin is an overseas collectivity of France with a territorial council and is part of the European Union as an outermost region.

economy.heading: Tourism
paragraphs: Tourism is the main industry, with beaches, restaurants and duty-free shopping. Unemployment is high and the economy is closely tied to the Dutch side. The currency is the euro, though US dollars are widely accepted.
